```text
**Minimum bar:** no running app (D1), no sprint report (D6), or no merged PRs (D5) ⇒ **0 for the
whole sprint**, regardless of everything else.

**Rules that constrain how AI is used here — these bind this agent:**

- **D5 concept location must be done by the human first, without AI.** The spec is explicit:
  "Find the relevant code yourself first, without AI ... Then confirm with AI ... This order
  matters." So when Zach is working a D5 issue, **do not locate the code for him** — wait until
  he states a hypothesis, then confirm, extend or disprove it. Offering the file path unasked
  defeats a graded learning objective.
- **He must be able to explain every line.** Prefer explaining and reviewing over generating;
  points are lost if he cannot explain his own PR.
- **Branch names**: `feat/issue-<n>-<slug>` or `fix/issue-<n>-<slug>`.
  **Commit messages**: the spec's own example is `feat: add dark mode toggle (#17)` —
  **Conventional Commits**, matching `AGENTS.md`, and *contradicting* the team's draft
  `standards.md` ("Add …"). The course spec and `main` agree; the draft is the outlier.
- **PRs**: link the issue with `Closes #<n>`, tests written/updated, reviewed by a teammate with
  an actual comment, CI passing (CI not required for Sprint 0). `main` is branch-protected.
- **AI logs** are captured with **SpecStory**, not written by hand.

### Settled: D1 — the app runs locally

Verified 2026-09-14 on Node 22.14.0. `./scripts/cal dev` brings it up (it starts Postgres,
ensures the database exists, then runs `yarn dev`).
```

```text
"use client";

import { createContext, useContext, useEffect, useMemo, useState } from "react";

import { trpc } from "@calcom/trpc/react";
import { showToast } from "@calcom/ui/components/toast";

interface WebPushContextProps {
  permission: NotificationPermission;
  isLoading: boolean;
  isSubscribed: boolean;
  subscribe: () => Promise<void>;
  unsubscribe: () => Promise<void>;
}

export const WebPushContext = createContext<WebPushContextProps | null>(null);

interface ProviderProps {
  children: React.ReactNode;
}

export function WebPushProvider({ children }: ProviderProps) {
  const [permission, setPermission] = useState<NotificationPermission>(() =>
```

Handed over. Here's the whole trace.

## The gate

[EventTypeLayout.tsx:279](apps/web/modules/event-types/components/EventTypeLayout.tsx:279) — the Save button already *is* wired correctly:

```tsx
disabled={!formMethods.formState.isDirty}
```

So this isn't a missing-guard bug. The form is genuinely dirty on mount. That reframes the issue: find who dirties it.

## The form

[useEventTypeForm.ts:141](packages/platform/atoms/event-types/hooks/useEventTypeForm.ts:141) creates it with `defaultValues` memoized from `eventType` ([:41](packages/platform/atoms/event-types/hooks/useEventTypeForm.ts:41)). Consumed by [EventTypeWebWrapper.tsx:173](apps/web/modules/event-types/components/EventTypeWebWrapper.tsx:173), passed down as `formMethods`.

Important constraint: [EventType.tsx:103](apps/web/modules/event-types/components/EventType.tsx:103) renders `{tabMap[tabName]}` — **only the active tab mounts**. Default tab on edit is `setup`, so the culprit has to live in the Setup tab.

## The culprit

[EventSetupTab.tsx:150-163](apps/web/modules/event-types/components/tabs/setup/EventSetupTab.tsx:150) renders the description `<Editor>` with:

```tsx
getText={() => md.render(formMethods.getValues("description") || "")}
setText={(value: string) => {
  const cleanedValue = value.replace(/&nbsp;/g, " ");
  const markdownValue = turndown(cleanedValue);
  formMethods.setValue("description", markdownValue, { shouldDirty: true });
}}
```

And [ToolbarPlugin.tsx:385-424](packages/ui/components/editor/plugins/ToolbarPlugin.tsx:385) — the mount effect (`useEffect(..., [])`) seeds the editor from `getText()`, then at [:410](packages/ui/components/editor/plugins/ToolbarPlugin.tsx:410) registers an update listener that calls `props.setText(...)` on **every** editor update, including Lexical's own normalization immediately after `$insertNodes`.

The chain, with no user input:

**stored markdown** → `md.render()` → HTML → Lexical nodes → `$generateHtmlFromNodes()` → `turndown()` → **markdown′**

That round trip is not identity — paragraph wrappers, `&nbsp;`/entity handling, and turndown's escaping all perturb it. `markdown′ !== defaultValues.description`, RHF marks `description` dirty, `isDirty` flips, line 279 un-disables Save.

## Ruled out

Three other mount-time `setValue(..., { shouldDirty: true })` effects exist; none can cause the reported symptom, because none is on the Setup tab:

| Location | Why not |
|---|---|
| [EventAvailabilityTab.tsx:456](apps/web/modules/event-types/components/tabs/availability/EventAvailabilityTab.tsx:456) | Availability tab. *Genuine* second bug — writes the default schedule id when `scheduleId` is unset. Worth its own issue. |
| [EventLimitsTab.tsx:342](packages/features/eventtypes/components/tabs/limits/EventLimitsTab.tsx:342) | Limits tab; value round-trips to the same minutes, so RHF un-dirties it. |
| [RequiresConfirmationController.tsx:57](apps/web/modules/event-types/components/tabs/advanced/RequiresConfirmationController.tsx:57) | Advanced tab; guarded by `!requiresConfirmation`. |

## Confirm it before you code

I traced this statically — I have **not** run it. One minute in the browser settles it:

```bash
./scripts/cal dev
```

Open an event type, and in the console watch whether `description` is the dirty field:

```js
document.querySelector('[data-testid="update-eventtype"]').disabled
```

Better: put a breakpoint in the `setText` callback at [EventSetupTab.tsx:157](apps/web/modules/event-types/components/tabs/setup/EventSetupTab.tsx:157). If it fires on load with nothing typed, that's it. Predicted: an event type with a **non-empty description** is dirty on load; one with an empty description is not. That asymmetry is the tell — and it's your fastest falsification test if I'm wrong.

## Fix directions — yours to pick

1. **Suppress the mount-time emission.** Ignore the first update-listener callback, or don't call `setText` until the editor has been focused/edited. Narrow, but touches shared UI used by workflows and elsewhere — check blast radius.
2. **Make the write non-dirtying at the source.** In `setText`, compare against `formMethods.getValues("description")` and skip the `setValue` when the normalized text is equivalent. Contained to the event-type tab.
3. **Normalize the default.** Store `defaultValues.description` already round-tripped so the first emission compares equal.

(2) is the smallest diff and the easiest to test; (1) is the more correct fix and the riskier one. Your PR, your call — and since you have to explain every line, pick the one you can defend.

For tests, [Editor.test.tsx](packages/ui/components/editor/Editor.test.tsx) already exists as a home if you go with (1); a component test asserting the Save button stays disabled after mount with a non-empty description is the more direct regression test for (2).
